findings.title: Stored XSS in booking receipt HTML via owner-controlled hotel/room fields
findings.attacker: Malicious or compromised hotel owner account
findings.controlled_input: Hotel name and room title set via owner property management forms (e.g. POST /api/owner/hotels/{id}, POST /api/owner/rooms/{id})
findings.attack_path: Owner stores HTML/JS in hotel.name or room.title → guest (or admin) with a confirmed booking opens GET /api/bookings/{id}/receipt in browser → response is text/html with unescaped ${hotel.name} and ${bookingRoomTitle(booking)} interpolated into the document → script executes on TajStay origin with the victim's session cookies sent on subsequent same-origin requests
findings.impact: Execute arbitrary JavaScript in the victim browser on the TajStay origin; perform authenticated API actions as the viewing guest/admin, manipulate UI, and exfiltrate page-visible booking data
findings.evidence: New route introduced in PR #36 builds HTML via template literal: `Отель${hotel.name}` and `Номер${bookingRoomTitle(booking)}` with Content-Type text/html and Content-Disposition inline. Owner hotel update accepts arbitrary name string with only .trim() at src/app/api/owner/hotels/[id]/route.ts. DownloadReceiptButton links directly to /api/bookings/{id}/receipt target=_blank.
findings.remediation: HTML-escape all dynamic fields before embedding in the receipt template, or generate receipts as text/PDF instead of raw HTML; consider a Content-Security-Policy on the response.

findings.title: Guest identity documents stored at publicly accessible upload URLs without authorization
findings.attacker: Any unauthenticated internet user who obtains or guesses a guest document URL
findings.controlled_input: Direct GET request to the stored guestDocumentUrl value (e.g. /uploads/guest-docs/{timestamp}-{uuid}.{ext} or a public Vercel Blob URL)
findings.attack_path: Authenticated guest uploads an identity document via POST /api/bookings/document → saveUploadFile writes to public/uploads/guest-docs on disk (or Vercel Blob with access public) and returns a world-readable URL stored in booking.guestDocumentUrl → attacker requests that URL directly with no session cookie → Next.js serves the file from public/ (or Blob CDN) with no ownership check
findings.impact: Exposure of guest identity documents (passport/ID scans); bypasses application PII controls such as offlinePrivacy masking because possession of the URL is sufficient for download
findings.evidence: document/route.ts calls saveUploadFile(file, "guest-docs", ...). saveUpload.ts saveToLocalDisk writes under process.cwd()/public/uploads/... and returns `/uploads/${normalized}/${name}`; saveToVercelBlob uses put(..., { access: "public" }). next.config.mjs does not restrict /uploads/*; offlinePrivacy.ts hides guestDocumentUrl from staff views but static URLs remain directly fetchable.
findings.remediation: Store guest documents in private storage (private Blob, S3 with auth, or private/ outside public/) and serve through an authenticated download route that verifies booking ownership/admin role; use signed short-lived URLs instead of permanent public links.

findings.title: Telegram login account takeover via unauthenticated webhook when TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset
findings.attacker: Remote unauthenticated attacker with any Telegram account
findings.controlled_input: Forged Telegram Bot API update JSON posted to POST /api/telegram/webhook (fake /start login_{token} and contact messages with victim phone number)
findings.attack_path: Attacker calls POST /api/auth/telegram/challenge to obtain token → when TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is empty the webhook skips secret verification → attacker posts forged /start login_{token} update binding their Telegram id → posts forged contact update with victim phone → attachPhoneAndSendCode stores OTP hash and sends the 6-digit code to attacker Telegram chat → attacker submits POST /api/auth/telegram/verify with token and code → createSessionCookie logs them into the existing account for that phone (or creates one)
findings.impact: Full account takeover of any phone number registered (or registerable) via Telegram login flow; access to bookings, chats, payments, and profile data for the hijacked account
findings.evidence: webhook/route.ts only checks x-telegram-bot-api-secret-token when sanitizeTelegramWebhookSecret(getTelegramWebhookSecret()) is truthy; otherwise all POST bodies are processed. loginChallenge.ts attachTelegramOnStart/attachPhoneAndSendCode trust webhook-supplied telegramId and phone. verify/route.ts issues a session on successful code verification. .env.example marks TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET as optional, unlike cron routes that fail closed without CRON_SECRET.
findings.remediation: Require TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET in production (return 503 if missing, mirroring cron/job routes) and reject all webhook POSTs without a matching x-telegram-bot-api-secret-token; additionally validate update integrity where possible.

findings.title: Payment proof receipts stored at publicly accessible upload URLs without authorization
findings.attacker: Any unauthenticated internet user who obtains or guesses a payment proof URL
findings.controlled_input: Direct GET request to booking.paymentProofUrl (e.g. /uploads/payment-proofs/{timestamp}-{uuid}.{ext}, a Vercel Blob CDN URL, or a chat attachment URL under /uploads/chat-attachments/{bookingId}/)
findings.attack_path: Authenticated guest uploads a bank transfer receipt via POST /api/payments/proof (or as a chat image in POST /api/chat/booking/{bookingId}/messages, which also sets paymentProofUrl) → saveUploadFile writes to public/uploads/payment-proofs or Vercel Blob with access public → URL is stored on the booking and shown to owner/admin in dashboard and PaymentReviewCard → attacker requests the URL directly with no session cookie → Next.js or the Blob CDN serves the file with no ownership check
findings.impact: Exposure of guest payment receipts and bank transfer screenshots containing account numbers, transaction IDs, and other financial PII; bypasses in-app access controls because possession of the URL is sufficient for download
findings.evidence: payments/proof/route.ts calls saveUploadFile(file, "payment-proofs", ...). saveUpload.ts saveToLocalDisk returns /uploads/{path} under public/ and saveToVercelBlob uses put(..., { access: "public" }). Chat messages route.ts also saves guest proof images via saveChatAttachmentFile → saveUploadFile and sets booking.paymentProofUrl. Owner dashboard and PaymentReviewCard render paymentProofUrl as a direct href/img src.
findings.remediation: Store payment proofs in private storage and serve through an authenticated download route that verifies booking ownership (guest/owner/admin); use signed short-lived URLs instead of permanent public links.

findings.title: Owner KYC passport documents uploaded with public Vercel Blob access despite private storage intent
findings.attacker: Any unauthenticated internet user who obtains an owner-application document blob URL
findings.controlled_input: Direct GET request to the HTTPS blob URL returned by savePrivateOwnerDoc (stored in OwnerApplication.passportFront, passportBack, selfieWithDoc, propertyDoc, or applicationMeta.uploads slots)
findings.attack_path: Guest submits an owner application via POST /api/owner/applications or POST /api/owner-requests with passport/KYC files → savePrivateOwnerDoc calls saveToPrivateBlob with put(..., { access: "public" }) despite the private-docs/ path prefix → full blob URL is persisted in the database → attacker obtains the URL (DB leak, log exposure, referrer, or insider) → unauthenticated GET to the blob CDN URL returns the passport/identity image with no admin session
findings.impact: Exposure of owner-applicant passport photos, selfies with documents, and property KYC files; the admin-only /api/admin/owner-requests/{id}/file proxy is bypassed entirely when the raw blob URL is known
findings.evidence: savePrivateFile.ts saveToPrivateBlob uses put(storageKeyPath, buffer, { access: "public", ... }) while comments state documents are saved outside /public and never as public URLs. owner/applications/route.ts and owner-requests/route.ts both call savePrivateOwnerDoc for passportFront/passportBack/selfie/propertyDoc. readPrivateFile.ts readPublicBlob fetches blob URLs without Authorization, confirming world-readable blobs.
findings.remediation: Upload owner KYC files with Vercel Blob private access (or non-public storage) and serve exclusively through the authenticated admin /file route; never persist world-readable blob URLs for sensitive documents.

findings.title: Authenticated users can hijack phone OTP login by changing profile phone without verification
findings.attacker: Any authenticated TajStay user (GUEST, OWNER, or ADMIN)
findings.controlled_input: Victim phone number in JSON body to POST /api/profile/phone
findings.attack_path: Attacker registers or logs into their own account → POST /api/profile/phone with victim phone → updateProfilePhone sets phone and phoneVerified:true without OTP → victim later completes POST /api/auth/phone-otp/verify for that phone → handlePhoneOtpVerify finds existing user by phone and issues session for attacker-controlled user id → attacker retains their original 7-day session cookie from step 1
findings.impact: Account takeover of victims who have not yet registered that phone; parallel sessions let attacker observe victim bookings, chats, uploaded identity documents, and payment proofs
findings.evidence: profile/phone/route.ts calls updateProfilePhone with no verification gate. updateFields.ts sets phoneVerified:true and verified:true synchronously. phoneOtpHandlers.ts lines 122-167 look up user by phone and call createSessionCookie for existing.id without checking whether phone was attacker-assigned.
findings.remediation: Require phone OTP verification before binding a new phone to an account; do not set phoneVerified until the victim proves possession of the number.

findings.title: Authenticated users can hijack Google OAuth sign-in by changing profile email without verification
findings.attacker: Any authenticated TajStay user
findings.controlled_input: Victim email address in JSON body to POST /api/profile/email
findings.attack_path: Attacker sets victim email on their account via POST /api/profile/email → updateProfileEmail stores email and sets emailVerified to current timestamp without sending a confirmation link → victim signs in with Google OAuth via /api/auth/[...nextauth] → Prisma adapter matches the existing verified-email user record (attacker account) → victim receives a session for attacker-controlled user id while attacker may retain a parallel session
findings.impact: OAuth account hijack; victim Google sign-in is routed into attacker-controlled account with access to victim-visible bookings, chats, and profile data; blocks legitimate separate registration for that email
findings.evidence: profile/email/route.ts calls updateProfileEmail with no verification step. updateFields.ts sets emailVerified:new Date() immediately. Google provider is registered in auth/[...nextauth]/route.ts and Auth.js links OAuth logins to users by verified email.
findings.remediation: Require email verification (magic link or OTP) before marking emailVerified; reject profile email changes until the inbox owner confirms.

findings.title: Unauthenticated booking flow squats victim phone numbers and issues attacker sessions
findings.attacker: Unauthenticated internet visitor
findings.controlled_input: Victim phone number (and booking fields) in POST /api/bookings form data
findings.attack_path: Attacker submits POST /api/bookings without session cookie using victim phone → route creates a new GUEST user for that phone with no OTP/SMS proof → booking is created and createSessionCookie issues a 7-day session to attacker → victim cannot register separately with that phone (unique constraint / phone_in_use) → when victim later uses phone OTP login they are authenticated into the squatted account while attacker session from step 2 remains valid
findings.impact: Phone-number preemption and shared-account takeover; attacker can create bookings and chats under victim phone identity and retain access to victim activity for up to seven days
findings.evidence: bookings/route.ts lines 84-103 create guest users without verification when sessionUser is null; lines 247-256 call createSessionCookie for the new user. session.ts sets 7-day TTL. phoneOtpHandlers.ts logs into existing user by phone without distinguishing squatted accounts.
findings.remediation: Require phone OTP verification before creating users or issuing sessions from the booking flow; do not auto-login unauthenticated bookers until the phone is verified.

findings.title: Hotel owner can forcibly promote any guest to global HOTEL_MODERATOR without consent
findings.attacker: Authenticated hotel OWNER with MANAGE_STAFF permission on a property
findings.controlled_input: Victim phone or userId in POST /api/owner/hotels/{hotelId}/moderators JSON body
findings.attack_path: Owner learns guest phone from a booking → POST /api/owner/hotels/{id}/moderators with {phone: victimPhone} → handler looks up guest user and globally updates user.role from GUEST to HOTEL_MODERATOR → hotelModerator row is upserted assigning victim to owner hotel → victim gains /api/moderator/* and /dashboard/moderator access on next login without accepting or being notified in this handler
findings.impact: Unauthorized privilege escalation and account modification; victim can be assigned moderator duties and perform offline booking, check-in, and calendar actions under their identity without consent
findings.evidence: moderators/route.ts lines 58-60 mutate global user.role for any GUEST target. No acceptance workflow or notification in handler. middleware.ts grants /dashboard/moderator to HOTEL_MODERATOR role via tajstay_role cookie.
findings.remediation: Keep moderator assignment hotel-scoped without changing global role, or require victim acceptance via invite token before role elevation.

findings.title: Default admin secret word tajstay-secret bypasses second factor on fresh deployments
findings.attacker: Attacker who has compromised the admin login password
findings.controlled_input: secretWord form field on POST /api/admin/security/update (value tajstay-secret or ADMIN_SECRET_WORD default)
findings.attack_path: On fresh deploy adminSecurityState has no secretWordHash → attacker logs in with stolen admin password → submits POST /api/admin/security/update with currentPassword and secretWord tajstay-secret → verifyAdminSecretWord falls back to plaintext comparison against defaultSecretWord() because stored hash is null → attacker changes admin phone, email, and password and rotates sessions
findings.impact: Persistent admin credential takeover when login password is compromised; documented default second factor provides no meaningful protection until an admin manually sets a new secret word
findings.evidence: admin-security.ts defaultSecretWord returns process.env.ADMIN_SECRET_WORD ?? tajstay-secret and verifyAdminSecretWord returns candidate === defaultSecretWord() when no hash exists. .env.example documents default tajstay-secret. assertProdSecrets in envGuard.ts does not validate ADMIN_SECRET_WORD. admin/security/update/route.ts requires secretWord in production and calls verifyAdminSecretWord.
findings.remediation: Require a strong random ADMIN_SECRET_WORD at deploy time, fail closed if no secretWordHash is stored, and add production guardrails similar to CRON_SECRET.

findings.title: Telegram login account takeover via sharing victim phone as contact card
findings.attacker: Remote attacker with any Telegram account
findings.controlled_input: Victim phone number supplied as message.contact.phone_number (any saved or forwarded Telegram contact card, not the attacker's own number)
findings.attack_path: Attacker starts POST /api/auth/telegram/challenge and opens /start login_{token} in the bot → instead of the request_contact button, attacker sends a contact card for the victim's phone → attachPhoneAndSendCode stores that phone on the challenge and emails the 6-digit OTP to the attacker's Telegram chat → attacker submits POST /api/auth/telegram/verify with token and code → resolveUserFromChallenge logs into the existing user for that phone and links attacker's telegramId
findings.impact: Full account takeover of any user whose phone number the attacker can attach to a Telegram contact message; access to bookings, chats, uploaded identity documents, and payment proofs even when TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is correctly configured
findings.evidence: webhookHandlers.ts lines 56-74 accept message.contact.phone_number with no check that contact.user_id equals message.from.id. loginChallenge.ts attachPhoneAndSendCode sends OTP via sendTelegramMessage to attacker chatId and resolveUserFromChallenge matches prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { phone } }). verify/route.ts issues createSessionCookie on success. Distinct from webhook-forgery finding because it uses legitimate Telegram updates.
findings.remediation: Reject contact messages unless contact.user_id is present and equals message.from.id; alternatively require Firebase/SMS phone verification before session issuance.

findings.title: Hotel owner can confirm unpaid online bookings without payment proof
findings.attacker: Authenticated hotel owner of the booked property
findings.controlled_input: bookingId in POST /api/owner/bookings/{id}/payment-approve
findings.attack_path: Guest creates an online booking (payOnArrival false, status WAITING_PAYMENT, no paymentProofUrl) → owner calls POST /api/owner/bookings/{bookingId}/payment-approve with their session cookie → confirmBookingPaymentOwner accepts WAITING_PAYMENT/WAIT_PROOF/ON_REVIEW without requiring paymentProofUrl or proofSubmittedAt → booking becomes CONFIRMED with paymentStatus PAID and payment CAPTURED
findings.impact: Owners can mark unpaid bookings as paid and confirmed, locking inventory, sending guest confirmation emails, and bypassing the admin proof-review workflow that requires ON_REVIEW plus an uploaded receipt
findings.evidence: ownerPaymentApprove.ts ALLOWED_STATUSES includes WAITING_PAYMENT and has no paymentProofUrl check before update to CONFIRMED/PAID. adminBookingActions.ts confirmBookingPaymentAdmin requires ON_REVIEW and paymentProofUrl. Owner dashboard renders OwnerPaymentApproveButton for WAITING_PAYMENT and WAIT_PROOF bookings (dashboard/owner/page.tsx lines 1232-1235) even when paymentProofUrl is absent.
findings.remediation: Align owner approval with admin rules: require ON_REVIEW status and a submitted paymentProofUrl before confirming; restrict early-status approval to explicit pay-on-arrival/offline flows only.

findings.title: CSRF on admin form mutations grants ADMIN role via victim admin session
findings.attacker: Remote attacker who hosts a malicious webpage
findings.controlled_input: HTML form fields (id, role, isBanned) auto-submitted via cross-site POST while a logged-in admin visits the attacker page
findings.attack_path: Victim admin browses attacker-controlled site → page auto-submits top-level POST form to /api/admin/users/update with attacker user id and role=ADMIN → browser sends tajstay_session cookie because SameSite=Lax allows cookies on cross-site top-level POST → handler calls getAdminUser() on victim session and updates prisma.user.role without CSRF token or Origin validation → attacker account becomes ADMIN and can use a parallel session
findings.impact: Full administrative takeover of the TajStay platform without knowing the admin password; attacker can access all user PII, approve hotels, modify bookings, and read owner KYC documents through admin APIs
findings.evidence: session.ts sets tajstay_session with sameSite lax and no CSRF middleware exists. admin/users/update/route.ts accepts req.formData() POST with only getAdminUser() check. Same pattern on other high-impact form routes: admin/users/credentials, admin/security/update, admin/hotels/moderate, admin/bookings/payment. NextAuth CSRF cookies are cleared on logout but legacy session auth has no synchronizer token.
findings.remediation: Add CSRF tokens to all cookie-authenticated mutations, validate Origin/Referer on POST, or set session cookies to SameSite=Strict; prefer JSON APIs with custom headers for sensitive admin actions.

findings.title: Owner KYC bypass via JSON owner-application API without mandatory identity uploads
findings.attacker: Authenticated GUEST account
findings.controlled_input: JSON body (fullName, phone, email, businessName, consent, etc.) sent with Content-Type application/json to POST /api/owner/applications
findings.attack_path: Attacker POSTs /api/owner/applications with application/json (not multipart) and valid jsonSchema fields → JSON branch creates ownerApplication with no passportFront, passportBack, selfieWithDoc, or propertyDoc columns → admin approves via PATCH /api/admin/owner-requests/{id} or POST /api/admin/owner-applications/{id}/approve → approveOwnerRequest promotes user.role to OWNER and auto-creates a hotel without any server-side document validation
findings.impact: Bypasses mandatory KYC upload controls enforced on the multipart path and /api/owner-requests; a fraudulent application can reach OWNER role and receive a hotel if an admin approves without noticing empty availableFileTypes
findings.evidence: applications/route.ts multipart branch (lines 168-179) requires identity/property photos; JSON branch (lines 244-290) calls prisma.ownerApplication.create with only text fields. owner-requests/route.ts rejects non-multipart at line 84-86. ownerRequestReview.ts approveOwnerRequest has no passport/document checks. Admin detail GET returns availableFileTypes via listOwnerRequestFileTypes which is empty for JSON submissions.
findings.remediation: Reject non-multipart submissions on /api/owner/applications or require the same mandatory file fields; block approveOwnerRequest unless required document refs exist.

findings.title: JOB_SECRET accepted in URL query string enables credential leakage via access logs
findings.attacker: Anyone with access to HTTP access logs (ops staff, compromised log aggregator, CDN/proxy logs)
findings.controlled_input: secret query parameter on POST /api/jobs/expire-bookings?secret=<JOB_SECRET>
findings.attack_path: Scheduler or operator invokes POST /api/jobs/expire-bookings?secret=<JOB_SECRET> → route accepts secret from req.nextUrl.searchParams.get("secret") as well as x-job-secret header → query strings are recorded in reverse-proxy, CDN, and APM logs → attacker extracts JOB_SECRET from logs → attacker calls the job endpoint to mass-expire WAITING_PAYMENT/WAIT_PROOF bookings and auto-reject timed-out ON_REVIEW payments
findings.impact: Privileged background job invocation after secret leakage; operational and financial disruption by cancelling unpaid bookings, sending cancellation emails, and failing associated payments
findings.evidence: expire-bookings/route.ts line 12: provided = req.headers.get("x-job-secret") ?? req.nextUrl.searchParams.get("secret"). Job updates bookings to EXPIRED/REJECTED, creates notifications, dispatches cancellation emails, and marks payments FAILED. Cron routes only accept Bearer header, not query params.
findings.remediation: Accept JOB_SECRET only via header (or signed JWT); reject query-string secrets and rotate JOB_SECRET if query usage occurred.

findings.title: Profile password change does not revoke existing sessions enabling persistent takeover
findings.attacker: Attacker holding any valid session cookie for the victim account (stolen cookie, shared device, or prior compromise)
findings.controlled_input: New password and confirm fields in JSON body to POST /api/profile/password
findings.attack_path: Attacker obtains victim tajstay_session (7-day TTL from session.ts) → victim later changes password via POST /api/profile/password believing access is revoked → updateProfilePassword only hashes and stores the new password with no session.deleteMany → attacker's original session remains valid until natural expiry while victim uses a new session from their next login
findings.impact: Persistent account access after victim password change; attacker retains up to seven days of authenticated access to bookings, chats, identity documents, and payment data
findings.evidence: profile/password/route.ts calls updateProfilePassword with no current-password check. updateFields.ts updateProfilePassword performs prisma.user.update on password only. Contrast auth/reset-password/route.ts lines 63-66 and 94-96 which run session.deleteMany({ where: { userId } }) in the same transaction as password update.
findings.remediation: Require current password or step-up OTP before change; on success delete all sessions for the user and issue a fresh session cookie (mirror reset-password behavior).

findings.title: Hotel moderator offline booking APIs bypass VIEW_FINANCES to read and mutate revenue fields
findings.attacker: Authenticated HOTEL_MODERATOR assigned to a hotel without VIEW_FINANCES permission
findings.controlled_input: totalPrice, prepayment, offlinePaymentType, and offlineNote in POST /api/moderator/offline-bookings and PATCH/POST /api/moderator/offline-bookings/{id}; unredacted booking rows returned by GET /api/moderator/offline-bookings
findings.attack_path: Owner assigns a hotel moderator whose MODERATOR_PERMISSIONS omit VIEW_FINANCES (permissions.ts) → dashboard UI hides finances via toOfflineOwnerView(..., canViewFinances=false) on moderator/page.tsx → moderator calls GET /api/moderator/offline-bookings (Accept: application/json) and receives raw prisma booking rows including totalPrice/prepayment via bookingWithHotelInclude → moderator POSTs a new offline booking with arbitrary totalPrice or PATCHes an existing booking to change revenue fields → handlers only call requireModeratorApiUser or requireBookingApiPermission(..., OFFLINE_BOOKING) with no VIEW_FINANCES gate
findings.impact: Staff explicitly denied financial visibility can read and alter booking revenue, prepayment, and payment-type data, enabling financial misreporting or fraud contrary to the RBAC model
findings.evidence: permissions.ts MODERATOR_PERMISSIONS (lines 36-45) excludes VIEW_FINANCES while including OFFLINE_BOOKING. offline-bookings/route.ts GET (lines 29-45) returns full booking entities; POST (lines 64-98) and [id]/route.ts PATCH (lines 44-50) accept totalPrice/prepayment without finance permission checks. offlinePrivacy.ts toOfflineOwnerView strips finances when canViewFinances=false, and moderator/page.tsx lines 163-165 pass canViewFinances={false} to OfflineBookingsList, but API responses bypass that masking.
findings.remediation: Redact totalPrice, prepayment, remainingAmount, and offlinePaymentType in moderator offline-booking API responses unless requireHotelApiPermission(hotelId, VIEW_FINANCES) passes; reject writes of financial fields without VIEW_FINANCES; apply the same server-side masking already used in dashboard rendering.

findings.title: Hotel moderator calendar API exposes per-booking totalPrice without VIEW_FINANCES
findings.attacker: Authenticated HOTEL_MODERATOR assigned to a hotel without VIEW_FINANCES permission
findings.controlled_input: GET /api/moderator/calendar with optional hotelId, roomId, and days query parameters
findings.attack_path: Moderator loads the calendar section or calls GET /api/moderator/calendar → requireModeratorApiUser passes with only HOTEL_MODERATOR role check → getModeratorCalendarData builds cellMeta entries with totalPrice: String(hit.totalPrice) for each occupied calendar cell → JSON response returns the full cellMeta map including per-booking revenue for all assigned hotels → moderator reads amounts without VIEW_FINANCES
findings.impact: Individual booking revenue figures are exposed to reception-style moderators who are meant to operate the calendar without financial visibility, undermining owner RBAC intent
findings.evidence: ownerCalendar.ts lines 205-216 always set totalPrice in cellMeta. calendar/route.ts lines 8-29 return the full calendar payload with no finance redaction. permissions.ts excludes VIEW_FINANCES from MODERATOR_PERMISSIONS. OwnerCalendar.tsx lines 473-479 render totalPrice from cellMeta in the detail drawer; moderator/page.tsx passes readOnly but does not suppress financial fields in API data.
findings.remediation: Omit totalPrice (and other finance fields) from cellMeta and calendar JSON when the caller lacks VIEW_FINANCES; enforce redaction server-side instead of relying on UI-only hiding.

findings.title: Payment-wait guest chat content leaked to owner via Pusher and web push alerts
findings.attacker: Authenticated guest on a booking in WAITING_PAYMENT or WAIT_PROOF status
findings.controlled_input: Chat message body and sender name submitted via POST /api/chat/booking/{bookingId}/messages
findings.attack_path: Guest posts a chat message while booking is WAITING_PAYMENT or WAIT_PROOF -> messages/route.ts calls notifyBookingChatMessage without status checks -> ownerId is always included in receiverIds -> createNotification stores full preview and sendWebPushToUser delivers it -> triggerUserNotifyEvent pushes user-alert to private-user-notify-{ownerId} -> owner browser ChatAlertsProvider shows system notification with full guest message text despite chat page and GET /api/chat/booking/{id}/messages filtering non-SYSTEM messages for owners in those statuses
findings.impact: Bypasses the ownerQuiet escrow policy; owner reads guest payment details, identity hints, or harassment during the admin verification window that the app explicitly hides elsewhere
findings.evidence: messages/route.ts lines 91-93 redact owner GET responses for WAITING_PAYMENT/WAIT_PROOF but lines 217-224 always call notifyBookingChatMessage after POST. bookingChatNotify.ts lines 48-76 add ownerId to receivers with no booking.status guard and embed preview in notification message, web push body, and Pusher USER_ALERT payload. chat/booking/[bookingId]/page.tsx lines 51-59 show ownerQuiet screen blocking chat UI for same statuses.
findings.remediation: Skip ownerId in notifyBookingChatMessage when booking.status is WAITING_PAYMENT or WAIT_PROOF; send generic alerts without message preview until ON_REVIEW.

findings.title: Payment-wait guest chat preview exposed to owner via inbox API
findings.attacker: Authenticated guest on a booking in WAITING_PAYMENT or WAIT_PROOF status
findings.controlled_input: Chat message body stored via POST /api/chat/booking/{bookingId}/messages
findings.attack_path: Guest sends chat message during payment-wait -> owner opens /dashboard/messages which calls GET /api/chat/inbox -> getInboxConversations returns lastMessage from chatMessages[0].body with no owner/status redaction -> MessagesInbox renders the guest message preview while owner is blocked from the dedicated chat page and redacted messages API
findings.impact: Owner reads guest chat content during the escrow verification period, undermining the same ownerQuiet confidentiality boundary enforced on the chat page and messages GET handler
findings.evidence: inbox.ts lines 134-162 set lastMessage from chatMessages[0].body without checking viewer role or booking.status. Contrast messages/route.ts lines 91-93 which filter non-SYSTEM messages for owners in WAITING_PAYMENT/WAIT_PROOF. MessagesInbox.tsx line-clamps lastMessage into the owner inbox list. ownerQuiet copy in messages.ts states chat details are unavailable until ON_REVIEW.
findings.remediation: When building inbox rows for OWNER viewers and booking.status is WAITING_PAYMENT or WAIT_PROOF, omit or replace lastMessage with a placeholder matching ownerQuiet policy.
